factors.name: Intention vs. accident
factors.description: Whether a person brings about an outcome on purpose or by accident; the physical act and the outcome are held fixed.

factors.name: Doing vs. allowing
factors.description: Whether a person actively brings about an outcome or merely allows it when they could have prevented it; outcome, knowledge, motive and ease of acting otherwise are held fixed.

factors.name: Knowledge vs. lucky true belief
factors.description: Whether a true, well-supported belief is true in the normal way or only by luck; the belief, its truth and the evidence as the person sees it are held fixed.

factors.name: Moral luck (outcome luck)
factors.description: Whether one and the same choice, made with the same knowledge and risk, happens to turn out harmlessly or harmfully for reasons outside the person's control.

factors.name: Norm violation and causal judgment
factors.description: Whether a person's contribution to an outcome broke a rule or was permitted, with the physical contribution held fixed; the judgment is how much that person caused the outcome.

factors.name: Null control
factors.description: An incidental detail that should not matter (control pairs only).

The rope snapped back, the gap opened, and Mrs. Vane fell onto the concrete and broke her hip. The ferry left on time. Tomas wrote the departure in the logbook. Tomas had been waiting for this. One evening, Jo switched on a 2,000-watt kettle in the kitchen at the same moment that Sam switched on a 2,000-watt hair dryer in the bathroom. Neither knew what the other was doing. The circuit tripped, the power went out, and by morning the food in the freezer had spoiled.

B.text: Jo and Sam share a flat with old wiring: the circuit trips if more than 3,000 watts are drawn at once. One evening, Jo turned on a 2,000-watt kettle in the kitchen at exactly the moment Sam turned on a 2,000-watt hair dryer in the bathroom. Each was unaware of what the other was doing. The circuit tripped, the power went out, and by morning the food in the freezer had spoiled.

judgment_question.text: How much do you agree with this statement: Jo caused the power outage.

comprehension_question.text: How many watts can the circuit carry before it trips?

pairs.intended_difference: Two sentences are reworded with the same meaning (‘switched on … at the same moment that’ / ‘turned on … at exactly the moment’; ‘Neither knew’ / ‘Each was unaware’). This should not matter.

prediction.rationale: Null control: a meaning-preserving rewording is irrelevant to causal judgment.
